zarr backend of the store layer (tables)

Source: R/io-store-zarr-table.R
io-store-zarr-table.Rd

The table_read and table_write operations of io-store for zarr v3, which hold the rec-array Element as a one-dimensional array of the struct data type. Rarr cannot read or write these, so the records are packed and unpacked in R and only the zstd and blosc steps go through Rarr (see zarr_compress() and zarr_decompress(), gzip is done in R).

Arguments

store

A zarr group node.

key, path

Name or path of the array.

frame

A data.frame of numeric, logical and character columns.

call

The call reported by errors.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options.

column, name

A column of frame and its name.

values, type, size

Strings of a field, its data type and its width in bytes.

Details

Python writes the fields in order, one record after another with no padding, little-endian, with strings as fixed_length_utf32 (zero padded) or null_terminated_bytes, and compresses each chunk as compressors says (zstd by default). Reading handles those codecs with zstd, gzip, blosc or no compression, and the chunk grid of any size. zarr keeps the field dtypes (zarr-io/14), as HDF5 does (see io-store-h5-table), and ignores the string records of HDF5. Reading records the dtype of each column that is not the R type, as for plain arrays: the numeric name ("uint8", "float32", ...) and for strings "<type>:<length_bytes>" unless it is the fixed_length_utf32 width that writing would choose. Writing restores the records, and sizes fields without one as Python does (int32, float64, bool, and fixed_length_utf32 of four times the longest UTF-8 byte length). Records are one chunk, sharded only when shards is given because Python's automatic sharding of rec-arrays is disabled.
